title: partner-beta-onboarding-pause-draft-jordan-patel
content:
TL;DR:
We need to pause new partner onboarding into the Q1 beta cohort effective immediately (target: pause window = 48 hours) while Legal + Security review a contract/data-handling clause flagged by Partner X. This is a short, contained hold; goal is to avoid surprises for partners and give GTM teams a consistent message.

Audience:
- Primary: partner success managers, partner sales reps, partner engineering liaisons
- Secondary: product + eng (oncall/PM), Legal, Security, CS leadership

Why: quick summary of facts to include in any comms
- Onboarding pause triggered by discovery of ambiguous language in the beta participation agreement around data retention and customer-provided prompt storage.
- Partner X surfaced the ambiguity during contract negotiation (redlined clause).
- Legal and Security requested a brief pause to align the contract language with our privacy guarantees and confirm technical controls.
- No incidents or data exposures — purely preventative/legal alignment.

Key objectives for messaging:
- Be transparent: partners should know "why" and "how long" (estimate).
- Reassure: no security incident; this is administrative/legal housekeeping.
- Provide timeline and next steps: what we expect in 48–72 hours and who to contact.
- Give partners a single authoritative contact (Partner Ops mailbox / named AM).

Draft subject lines (short variants for email/DM):
- "Temporary pause on new beta onboardings — short update from Redwood"
- "Quick update: beta onboarding temporarily on hold"

Draft partner email body (friendly, short):
Hi <PartnerName>,

Quick heads-up: we're pausing new onboardings into the Q1 beta for a short period (anticipated 48–72 hours) while our legal and security teams finalize a small clarification to the beta agreement related to data handling.

What this means for you:
- If you're already in the pipeline, your point of contact will reach out with next steps — no action required.
- If you have an active SOW or signed agreement, we will continue with the current plan unless we explicitly reach out.
- We do not expect any disruption to the product or to partners already live.

We expect to have the updated language and an internal FAQ ready within 48 hours. Please direct any contract-specific questions to partner-ops@redwood.com and cc <AM name>.

Appreciate your patience — we want to get the wording right so there are no surprises down the road.

Best,
Jordan

Internal Q&A / prep for AMs (anticipated partner questions + suggested replies)
Q: Is this because of a security incident?
A: No — no incident. This is a precaution to ensure the agreement language accurately reflects how we handle customer-provided content and retention in the beta.

Q: Will this change the timeline for our integration?
A: For partners mid-onboarding we do not anticipate delays. If next steps are needed we'll reach out with a clear plan. For new prospects we will pause scheduling until the short review completes.

Q: Who authorized the pause?
A: Legal requested the review; GTM and Product supported the decision to pause proactively. Leadership (VPs in GTM/Product) are aware.

Q: Could this lead to broader product changes?
A: Unlikely. This is contract/wording-focused, not a product policy change. If Security requires a technical control change, we'll communicate separately.

Ops checklist for immediate actions (owners in parentheses)
- Send hold notice to active partner prospects (AMs) within 2 hours of decision (AM team).
- Update partner portal status page with short note + link to contact (Partner Ops / Marketing).
- Open a guarded Slack thread for AMs to forward partner-specific asks (channel: #partners-ops-hold) (Jordan).
- Ask Legal to produce a redline and a short FAQ doc for AMs (Legal: Aisha).
- Inform Engineering oncall/PM in case partners flag technical gating questions (PM: Marta).
- Create a single shared doc (confluence) with final FAQ and approved lines once Legal signs off (Marketing to publish).

Slack announcement (short):
Heads up — brief pause on new partner beta onboardings while Legal/Security review a contract clause. No security incident. AMs: please hold new scheduling requests and escalate any urgent partner timelines to me (Jordan) and Aisha.

Comms escalations: who to loop in by scenario
- Legal wording confirmed: publish updated FAQ (loop Marketing).
- Partner demands SLA exceptions: escalate to GTM leadership + Legal.
- Partner threatens to withdraw pilot: escalate to Head of Partnerships and CS leadership.

Unresolved questions / risks to flag
- If Legal requires a material change to data handling, we may need to update onboarding scripts and a short technical mitigation plan. Time to resolve could extend beyond 72 hours. (RISK: medium)
- Partners already signed under ambiguous wording — need to determine if re-signing is required. (Legal to advise)
- Impact on pipeline metrics (GTM) — track any conversion drop-offs during pause.

Approval path before outbound to partners
- Legal (required) -> Security (ack) -> Head of Partnerships (FYI) -> VP GTM (final signoff for partner-facing language).

Draft AM talking points (for quick calls)
- "We're pausing new onboardings for 48–72 hours to clarify a contract paragraph. No incident, we want to make sure the agreement matches our day-to-day handling of partner content."
- "You don't need to take any action; your AM will reach out if anything changes."
- "If you're under time pressure, tell us — we'll escalate internally and prioritize."

Publishing timeline (ideal):
- T0: Decision to pause (now) -> hold notice to AMs (within 2 hours)
- T+6–12h: Legal provides redline draft for AM FAQ
- T+24h: Internal FAQ + Slack channel open + partner portal stub updated
- T+48–72h: Final wording approved and outbound message sent to queued partners with next steps

TODOs (action items)
- [ ] Jordan: draft short email templates for AMs (personalized)
- [ ] Aisha: produce legal redline + short FAQ answers to the top 8 likely questions
- [ ] Marta: confirm if any integrations in-flight would be blocked by wording change
- [ ] Marketing: prepare partner portal blurb and an internal one-pager for AMs
- [ ] Partner Ops: compile list of queued partners and assign AM owner to each

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep messages minimal and non-alarming. Emphasize reassurance.
- Avoid overly legalese lines in initial partner comms — use plain English.
- We will not share internal legal details; provide partner-facing summary only.

If approvers agree, I'll assemble a polished partner email + AM playbook for distribution.
